title: Divide Intervals Into Minimum Number of Groups
summary: Given a 2D integer array intervals where each element intervals[i] is an array representing the inclusive interval [lefti, righti], determine the minimum number of groups needed such that no two intervals in the same group overlap.
statement: Given a 2D integer array intervals where each element intervals[i] is an array representing the inclusive interval [lefti, righti], determine the minimum number of groups needed such that no two intervals in the same group overlap. Each interval must be placed in exactly one group, and intervals are considered to overlap if they share any common number.
constraints: Intervals are inclusive, so intervals sharing an endpoint overlap.
Place every interval into a group whose intervals are pairwise non-overlapping.
Return the minimum number of groups.
hints: Keep a min-heap of the ending value for each active group.
Reuse the earliest-ending group only when its end is strictly less than the new start; otherwise open another group.
The heap size equals simultaneous overlap, a lower bound, and earliest-ending reuse attains that bound.
editorial: The heap size equals simultaneous overlap, a lower bound, and earliest-ending reuse attains that bound.

tests.explanation: At value 6, three intervals overlap, requiring three groups; three groups also suffice.
Each interval ends before the next begins, so all fit in one group.
